}}The '''2021–22 Süper Lig''', officially called the '''Spor Toto Süper Lig [[Ahmet_Yılmaz_Çalık#Death|Ahmet Çalık]] season''',<ref>{{cite news|title=Spor Toto Süper Lig'e Ahmet Çalık Sezonu ismi verildi|url=https://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=285&ftxtID=36896|publisher=[[Turkish Football Federation]]|access-date=18 January 2022|language=tr|archive-date=18 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220118153628/https://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=285&ftxtID=36896|url-status=live}}</ref> was the 64th season of the [[Süper Lig]], the highest tier [[Association football|football]] league of [[Turkey]].

[[Trabzonspor]] clinched their seventh league title, and a first since the [[1983–84 1.Lig|1983–84 season]], on 30 April 2022, following 2–2 draw against [[Antalyaspor]]. With three weeks in the season still to spare, this equalled the earliest championship record set by [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]].

==Teams==
A total of 20 teams contested the league, including 17 sides from the [[2020–21 Süper Lig|2020–21 season]] and [[2020–21 TFF First League]] champions [[Adana Demirspor]], runner-ups [[Giresunspor]] and play-off winners [[Altay S.K.|Altay]]. Adana Demirspor returned top level after 26 years, Giresunspor returned after 44 years and Altay after 18 years.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.dailysabah.com/sports/football/adana-demirspor-giresunspor-earn-turkish-super-lig-promotion |title=Adana Demirspor, Giresunspor earn Turkish Süper Lig promotion |access-date=2021-05-29 |archive-date=2021-06-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602213607/https://www.dailysabah.com/sports/football/adana-demirspor-giresunspor-earn-turkish-super-lig-promotion |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.dailysabah.com/sports/football/izmir-club-altay-grabs-last-ticket-to-turkish-super-lig |title=Izmir club Altay grabs last ticket to Turkish Süper Lig |access-date=2021-05-29 |archive-date=2021-06-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602212408/https://www.dailysabah.com/sports/football/izmir-club-altay-grabs-last-ticket-to-turkish-super-lig |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.trtspor.com.tr/haber/futbol/tff-1-lig/canli-izle-altinordu-altay-233422.html |title=Süper Lig'in son bileti Altay'ın (in Turkish) |access-date=2021-05-29 |archive-date=2021-06-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602213055/https://www.trtspor.com.tr/haber/futbol/tff-1-lig/canli-izle-altinordu-altay-233422.html |url-status=live }}</ref> For the first time in 40 years, there was no team from the capital city, Ankara. 
The bottom four teams were relegated to the [[TFF First League|2022–23 TFF First League]].
